title: Control Axis: 13-Layer Cr-Embedded Dielectric Stack with Refined Cr Bounds
scientific_hypothesis: A 13-layer stack with a thin Cr layer at index 2, sandwiched between HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave pairs tuned for 1000 nm, will maximize Visible absorption while maintaining NIR reflectance, and constraining Cr thickness to [10, 18] nm will improve optimization convergence.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge of thin-film interference: dielectric pairs with optical thickness ~lambda/4 at 1000 nm create high reflectance in NIR; a thin semi-transparent metal layer (Cr) absorbs Visible light while allowing IR to reflect off the underlying stack/substrate; bounding the metal thickness prevents it from becoming opaque (blocking IR reflection) or too thin (insufficient absorption).
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Al
design_variables: thicknesses_nm (13 variables, one per film layer)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 13 (within 20-layer limit)
Cr thickness constrained to [10, 18] nm for stability
theory_basis: Recalled rule of thumb: Quarter-wave stacks centered at 1000 nm use ~125 nm HfO2 (n~2.0) and ~170 nm SiO2 (n~1.45).
Recalled behavior: Cr films < 20 nm are semi-transparent in Visible but reflective in IR when backed by a mirror.
Recalled design pattern: Embedding the absorber near the front reduces parasitic absorption in the rear stack.
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to narrowed Cr search space
Higher IR reflectance due to explicit quarter-wave tuning in first two layers
known_risks: Material name 'cr' is not in the provided guaranteed_names list; local resolution must succeed.
Recalled quarter-wave thicknesses are approximate; actual n/k dispersion may shift optimal values.
Fixed topology may miss better configurations with Cr at different depths.
Uncertainty in whether 13 layers is optimal vs 14 or 12; this route does not explore layer count.
execution_request_english: Optimize a 13-layer planar multilayer stack on an Al (Rakic-LD) substrate under air incidence. Material sequence: Layer 1=HfO2, Layer 2=SiO2 (Lemarchand), Layer 3=Cr (Rakic-LD), Layer 4=HfO2, Layer 5=SiO2 (Lemarchand), Layer 6=HfO2, Layer 7=SiO2 (Lemarchand), Layer 8=HfO2, Layer 9=SiO2 (Lemarchand), Layer 10=HfO2, Layer 11=SiO2 (Lemarchand), Layer 12=HfO2, Layer 13=SiO2 (Lemarchand). Design variables are the thicknesses of these 13 layers. Bounds: Layer 3 (Cr (Rakic-LD)) must be between 10.0 and 18.0 nm. All other layers must be between 50.0 and 300.0 nm. Wavelength bands: 400-700 nm (target: maximize absorptance), 700-2000 nm (target: maximize reflectance). Polarization: unpolarized. Angle: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Solver: coherent TMM. Objective: maximize weighted sum of mean absorptance (400-700 nm) and mean reflectance (700-2000 nm).
revision_reason: Refined Cr layer thickness bounds to [10.0, 18.0] nm based on prior control iteration observations of optimal clusters, while maintaining the same 13-layer topology and material sequence.
